records.prompt:
Count how many times the word "data" appears in the text below, case-insensitive, whole words only ("dataset" does not count). Submit the integer.

The pipeline ingests raw data from three sources and writes cleaned data to the warehouse. Data quality checks run hourly; when a check fails the offending data is quarantined. Dashboards read aggregated data views, while analysts export raw data snapshots for ad hoc studies. Every dataset carries a schema version, and the data team reviews schema migrations weekly before any new data lands.

Dashboards read aggregated data views, while analysts export raw data snapshots for ad hoc studies. Every dataset carries a schema version, and the data team reviews schema migrations weekly before any new data lands.'
count = len([word for word in text.lower().split() if word == 'data'])
print(count)

records.prompt:
Given the list

[132, 820, 698, 808, 155, 864, 620, 101, 421, 630, 649, 174, 434, 889, 305, 175, 966, 679, 768, 766, 779, 468, 620, 809, 321, 189, 175, 28, 315, 275, 920, 976, 346, 892, 50, 498, 841, 70, 490, 578]

compute the running maximum (for each position, the maximum of all values up to and including it). Submit the 40 values as one comma-separated line, e.g. "29,29,41,41".

args.code:
numbers = [132, 820, 698, 808, 155, 864, 620, 101, 421, 630, 649, 174, 434, 889, 305, 175, 966, 679, 768, 766, 779, 468, 620, 809, 321, 189, 175, 28, 315, 275, 920, 976, 346, 892, 50, 498, 841, 70, 490, 578]

running_max = []
current_max = float('-inf')
for number in numbers:
    if number > current_max:
        current_max = number
    running_max.append(current_max)

print(','.join(map(str, running_max)))
